Carvana Co. (SEC filing data, standardized by Fiscal.ai)

credit_ratings.summary: S&P Global Ratings affirmed Carvana's BB- issuer credit rating and positive outlook; it rated the proposed $1.0 billion senior secured term loan BB with Recovery Rating 2. The issuer rating and positive outlook were unchanged.
Fitch assigned Carvana a first-time BB- Long-Term IDR with Stable Outlook; secured notes were rated BB+/RR2 and unsecured notes BB-/RR4.
Moody's upgraded Carvana's long-term rating to B1 from B2 and assigned a positive outlook.
Moody's assigned a B1 rating to Carvana's $1.66 billion senior secured term loan; the issuer's latest reported corporate-family rating remained B1 with positive outlook.

debt_events.summary: Carvana entered a credit agreement for a $1.66 billion senior secured Term Loan B maturing August 14, 2033. Proceeds were intended to redeem, repay or refinance the 2030 senior secured notes; the facility has no financial covenant.

Carvana amended its Ally Master Purchase and Sale Agreement to increase Ally's commitment to purchase up to $8.0 billion of finance-receivable principal balances during July 27, 2026 through July 26, 2027.

The Q2 2026 Form 10-Q disclosed a seventh $500 million revolving facility for finance receivables, available through November 8, 2027; as of June 30, 2026 finance-receivable facilities had zero drawn and $4.1 billion unused capacity.
Carvana reported that it was in compliance with all debt covenants and that the Form 10-Q's Defaults Upon Senior Securities item was None.

Fitch identified Carvana's 2023 distressed debt exchange as part of its credit history; the 2026 Fitch rating reflects subsequent profitability and leverage improvement but this remains a relevant restructuring precedent.

payment_behaviour.summary: Connecticut's Attorney General announced a $1.5 million settlement after hundreds of consumer complaints, including delayed payments to sellers, untimely loan payoffs, and a failed wire/check payment allegation. The settlement established $1.0 million of restitution and a $500,000 state penalty, subject to court approval.

distress_signals.summary: Fitch flags structural credit risks rather than an immediate default: customer-loan sales represented 56% of 2025 EBITDA, Carvana is a controlled company with related-party transactions, and access to securitization/loan buyers is important to liquidity. Fitch also notes the 2023 distressed debt exchange.

ownership.value: Public company (NYSE: CVNA), founder/family-controlled by Ernest Garcia II and Ernest Garcia III; Fitch states the Garcia family controls around 83% of voting rights. Ernest Garcia III is CEO. The 2026 proxy states the Garcia Parties retain 10 votes per Class B share while they meet the applicable ownership condition.

output.risk_rationale: Carvana's near-term debt-service capacity looks workable: at 2026-06-30 it reported $2.63 billion of cash, $7.024 billion of total liquidity resources against $5.1 billion of principal indebtedness, and no covenant breach or default disclosure; Q2 also produced $769 million of adjusted EBITDA [3](#cite-3) [2](#cite-2). Risk is not low because the issuer remains sub-investment-grade (S&P BB-, Fitch BB-, Moody's B1), relies heavily on customer-loan monetization, is tightly controlled by the Garcia family, has a 2023 distressed-exchange precedent, and has a documented history of delayed seller payments and loan payoffs [Fitch](https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-assigns-first-time-idr-of-bb-to-carvana-co-outlook-stable-30-07-2026) [CT Attorney General](https://portal.ct.gov/ag/press-releases/2025-press-releases/attorney-general-tong-announces-settlement-with-carvana-following-hundreds-of-consumer-complaints). The August 2026 term-loan refinancing and expanded Ally receivables commitment improve maturity/liquidity flexibility, but continued access to loan buyers and securitization markets remains important [SEC 8-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000059/cvna-20260814.htm) [SEC 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1690820/000169082026000055/cvna-20260630.htm).
